abstract: Background: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci associated with osteoarthritis (OA); however, the regulatory variants and effector genes underlying most associations remain unresolved. Results: We used complementary functional genomic approaches in chondrocytes to resolve prioritized OA risk loci. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) in primary human chondrocytes identified allele-specific regulatory activity at variants across multiple loci, two of which were independently validated using low-throughput reporter assays. In parallel, integration of OA GWAS signals with chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac CUT&Tag, and chromatin conformation data prioritised candidate regulatory elements for CRISPR based perturbation. CRISPR activation and interference supported functional regulatory relationships between OA risk regions and Pappalysin 1 (PAPPA) and Sprouty RTK signaling antagonist 4 (SPRY4) as target genes. At the 9q33 locus, multiple independent lines of evidence converged on rs1895062, which resides in an accessible region that loops to the PAPPA promoter. The OA risk G allele at rs1895062 results in higher regulatory activity by MPRA and low throughput reporter assay. Activation of this region by CRISPR increases PAPPA gene expression and induces widespread transcriptional changes involving extracellular matrix remodelling and other OA-relevant pathways. Conclusion: Integrating genetic association, genomic and epigenomic data, and functional perturbation in disease-relevant cells can resolve the regulatory mechanisms underlying OA risk loci. Using this multi-faceted approach, we provide convergent functional evidence for rs1895062 as a likely causal variant that controls PAPPA gene expression and OA risk.
